solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Current run taken by Scottish philosopher

parts.note: James Mill, the Scottish philosopher and father of John Stuart Mill
to run is to race

explanation.surface: A jogging event is enlisted by a Scottish thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is the noun: a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel whose flowing stream of water drives a mill wheel.

clue.text: Part of grain provided for breakfast, perhaps

definitions.meaning: breakfast is one example of a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Meal is ground cereal such as oatmeal, and also any occasion of eating, breakfast being one.

clue.text: Immature form of life right in centre of volcanic discharge

indicators.note: in centre of means the letter for right goes into the middle of the word for the discharge

parts.note: lava is what a volcano pours out

explanation.surface: A young creature survives at the heart of an eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in centre of' puts R in the middle of LAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young stage of an insect before it changes into its adult shape.

clue.text: Harshly made fewer advances in bank

indicators.note: in means the phrase for fewer loans goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
lent less means made smaller or fewer loans

explanation.surface: A bank cruelly cut back its lending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LENT LESS inside RELY, the verb sense of bank (bank on).
explanation.definitionFit: Relentlessly means without mercy or let-up, an unforgiving manner.

clue.text: Like bread — inferior, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the slang word for inferior is taken as heard, spelt differently

parts.note: crummy is slang for poor quality

explanation.surface: Bread that seems to be second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumby means full of or covered in crumbs, the bits that fall from a loaf.

clue.text: Young creature identified by US city doctor

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An American physician identifies a young animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is a young sheep, a baby animal.

clue.text: In pieces, in the manner indicated below

parts.note: as means in the way or manner
under means below, as in a note saying see under

explanation.surface: Something is in fragments, as shown further down the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart, torn into separate parts.

clue.text: Pestered, wanting emblem of bright colour

parts.note: a badge is an emblem worn to show membership
red is a bright colour

explanation.surface: Someone nagged for a vivid insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgered means harassed with repeated demands, as one nagged.

clue.text: Separation of weird blokes in Egypt's borders

indicators.note: in means the strange men go inside the edges of Egypt
borders means only the first and last letters of Egypt are used

parts.note: weird means strange
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Odd men on Egypt's frontier cause a rift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' means the outermost letters of Egypt only, ignoring the possessive; 'in' sets the odd men between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the state of being alienated or apart from someone once close.

clue.text: Report of examination relating to the ears

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for the examination is taken as it sounds

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An exam result concerns hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' looks like a school report but signals a word said out loud: ORAL sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural is the adjective for hearing, from the Latin for ear.

clue.text: A French waterway lacking security?

parts.note: un is French for a
a sound is a narrow sea channel

explanation.surface: A French canal is said to be poorly protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsound is unstable or not safe, so it is without a secure footing.

clue.text: TV inspector impolite about good Dickensian halfwit

parts.note: Inspector Barnaby is the detective in the British TV series Midsomer Murders

indicators.note: about means the word for impolite goes around the letter for good

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: A television detective is rude about a foolish Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is the simple-minded title character of a novel by Charles Dickens.

clue.text: Dull ship's officer, one sharing apartment

parts.note: flat means dull or lifeless
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A boring officer at sea shares lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone you live with in a shared flat, the British word for apartment.

clue.text: Liberal at site of cathedral in the recent past

parts.note: Ely is a small English city famous for its cathedral

explanation.surface: A Liberal recently visited a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately is an adverb for recently, not long ago.

clue.text: Trade in motor vehicles?

definitions.meaning: the vehicles moving on a road

explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means dealing in goods, and also the flow of cars and lorries on roads.

clue.text: Menu item's recent re-emergence, somewhat reduced

indicators.note: somewhat reduced says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dish has lately come back on the menu, in smaller portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat reduced' says the answer sits inside 'recent re-emergence', with the trimmed ends removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a course on a menu, a main dish or starter.

clue.text: Mostly own an area in Caribbean capital

indicators.note: mostly means the word for own loses its last letter

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone holds most of a plot in a Caribbean city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the E of HAVE to give HAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital city of Cuba, in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Openness familiar to photographers

definitions.meaning: the quality of being open and honest

explanation.definitionFit: Transparency means candour; it is also a positive image on film viewed by light passing through it.

clue.text: Is Capone able to identify a watercourse?

parts.note: is able is can, so the question is Capone able reads can Al
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A query about whether the gangster can find a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is Capone able' turned into a question is 'Can Al?'
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway for boats or irrigation.

clue.text: He entertains the Queen in this place

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or take in, so he goes around the Queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A man hosts the monarch at his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is read as its own letters, opened up to take in the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Here is the adverb for at this location.

clue.text: A couple of blokes introducing a form of forage

indicators.note: introducing means the two blokes come in front of the letter that follows

parts.note: two blokes each called Alf, a typical man's name, side by side

explanation.surface: Two men present a type of animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Alf is a stock crossword name for any bloke; two of them, then the final 'a', make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, also called lucerne, is a plant grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Chap showing interest at first in bird of prey

indicators.note: in means the first letter of interest goes inside the word for the bird

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of interest is used

explanation.surface: A man shows curiosity about an eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes I from 'interest'; 'in' puts it inside ERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's first name, and chap means a man.

clue.text: Make an impression, and so on, with husband

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and so on

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make their mark, along with a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design, cutting marks into a surface.

clue.text: Graduate motionless beside European fortress

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
motionless means still

explanation.surface: A graduate stands frozen next to a European castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789.
